summary: Pinned model 'ghosting' after canary rollover due to edge queue merge
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that after a staged canary rollover the tenant continued to receive traffic routed to a pinned model variant that should have been unpinned. This manifested as mixed responses: some sessions returned the promoted canary variant, others returned the old pinned variant even though rollout completed and pin TTLs had expired.

Impact: Affected one enterprise customer (PaperTrail AI) on dedicated capacity in us-east-1. Observed increased 400-level semantic-mismatch errors in application logs and customer complaints about inconsistent model behavior. Service remained generally healthy (no 5xx), but quality regressions for ~8% of requests to the tenant.

Environment: prod, dedicated pool for PaperTrail AI, region us-east-1, model gpt-redwood-v1-medium, canary rollout completed at ~2026-03-11T03:12:00Z.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a weighted canary rollout (10% -> 100%) for gpt-redwood-v1-medium on the tenant route with session affinity enabled.
2) During the weight increase there was a brief spike in edge retries due to a downstream CDN blip.
3) Edge proxies merged queued requests during retry collapse window and then reissued batched requests to routing service.
4) After rollout completed, some sessions continued to be routed to the earlier pinned variant for up to ~90 minutes despite pin TTL expiry.

Observed logs and evidence:
- Edge logs show retry bursts and queue-merge events between 03:05:xx and 03:08:xx UTC.
- Routing service trace (trace id: trace-20260311-8b9c) shows rehydrated session tokens that lacked the updated cohort assignment header.
- Canary-coordinator audit shows commit completed at 03:12:00Z and pin TTLs updated to expire at 03:13:00Z.
- Customer application traces show mixed model fingerprints (hashes) within the same 5-minute window.

Initial hypothesis: Edge retry-induced queue merging collapsed multiple in-flight requests that contained stale session affinity headers. When the merged batch was re-submitted the routing service applied a legacy pin-decision path due to a short-circuit in the routing cache invalidation logic, creating a 'ghost' pin that outlived TTLs.
comments: 2026-03-11T10:22:00Z - Priya Nair (Support): Escalating after customer reported inconsistent model outputs post-rollout. Customer attached sample request IDs and model fingerprints.
2026-03-11T11:05:00Z - Liam Chen (SRE): Noted edge retry spike in logs; creating temporary route filter to force fresh cohort assignment for affected tenant. Requesting routing traces for the window.
2026-03-11T13:40:00Z - PaperTrail AI (Customer): Confirming that forcing new session tokens temporarily normalized behavior. They observed ghosting for ~30-90 minutes after rollout.

2026-03-12T02:18:00Z - Mei Alvarez (Routing Eng): Reproduced race in staging with synthetic retries and queue-merge; routing cache invalidation was not triggered for merged batch path. Preparing a fix to ensure merged-batch replays consult latest cohort assignment store.
2026-03-13T09:12:00Z - Liam Chen (SRE): Deployed a canary fix to routing-service in staging (PR linked). Monitoring for any regressions. Planning hotfix for prod if staging looks good.
investigation_notes: Edge proxies implement a local merge optimization: when several near-identical requests are queued during a retry window they are collapsed into a single reissue to reduce load. This optimization did not previously consider session-affinity header freshness.

Trace analysis: merged requests reissued at edge had X-Session-Cohort header from the oldest request in the group. Routing-service cache key used (tenant + session-id) but not the cohort timestamp, allowing stale mapping to be applied.
Canary-coordinator confirmed commit and TTL expiry. No rollback or manual pin manipulation observed on control plane during window.

SRE reproduced scenario in staging by injecting a 200-300ms CDN retry burst while ramping canary weight. Confirmed routing-service path that services merged-batch requests bypasses the cohort-store refresh in ~12% of replays.
Impact quantification: roughly 6-9% of tenant traffic during spike windows subject to ghost pinning; overall session-level probability decays with session renewal.
resolution:
Workaround applied: forced cohort refresh for the tenant via routing-service admin call and invalidated edge merge cache for 60 minutes, which returned traffic to expected variant within ~10 minutes. Permanent fix merged and deployed to staging: routing-service now includes cohort timestamp in cache key and forces store refresh for merged-batch replays. Edge proxies updated to tag merged requests with the newest header when available.

Follow-ups:
- Prod rollout of routing-service fix scheduled for 2026-03-15 with 1% -> 100% canary and additional instrumentation.
- Add automated test in CI to simulate retry-collapse + canary rollouts.
- Documented mitigation steps in Confluence runbook and updated 'edge merge' operational notes.
- Postmortem scheduled: owners (Liam Chen, Mei Alvarez), due 2026-03-22.
